findings.asked: Balance the symbol equation for sodium with hydrochloric acid using the spaces provided.
findings.wentWrong: Many balanced it, but some changed the formulae instead of putting numbers in the spaces.
findings.rule: Balance with large numbers in front; never alter a formula.

findings.asked: Write a balanced symbol equation for a Group 1 metal with water.
findings.wentWrong: A large number stopped at the first marking point, and many wrote sodium oxide as the product.
findings.rule: Group 1 metal + water gives the hydroxide + hydrogen: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2.

findings.asked: A less familiar balanced equation with sodium carbonate as a product.
findings.wentWrong: Extra substances were added to the left-hand side and the formula of sodium carbonate was often wrong, so the standard was lower than for the familiar equation.
findings.rule: Only the substances named in the question appear; write each formula from its ions before balancing.

findings.asked: Balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for lithium reacting with water.
findings.wentWrong: Wrong formulae, wrong balancing numbers and wrong state symbols all appeared; the QWC on the same reactions also produced potassium oxide instead of the hydroxide.
findings.rule: Three separate checks: formulae, balance, state symbols (s, l, g, aq).

findings.asked: Balance an equation involving calcium oxide.
findings.wentWrong: The commonest error was to 'balance' by rewriting CaO as CaO2.
findings.rule: If the formula changes, the substance changes - it is no longer balancing.

ruleToRemember: Three marks: correct reactant formulae, correct product formulae, then balance with numbers in front (never inside) a formula. Metals with water give the hydroxide and hydrogen. Add state symbols only when asked, and get them right: aqueous for anything dissolved.
aStarSignal: Writing and balancing an unfamiliar equation from a description of the reactants and products, with every formula built from ions or valency.
